title: Open–closed reduction for the direct-image assertion
statement:
For a separated finite-type morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ of separated
finite-type $k_0$-schemes, say that $f_0$ satisfies the
*direct-image assertion* if, for every $w\in\mathbf R$ and every
constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ which is $\iota$-mixed of
weights at most $w$ ([def-weil-punctual-weights]), the sheaf
$R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+r$ for
every $r$; say that $f_0$ satisfies the *complex form* of the assertion
if $Rf_{0!}$ carries $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ into $D_{\le w}(Y_0)$ for every
$w$ ([def-weil-complex-weights]).

1. *(Source.)* Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be open with closed
   complement $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$. If the direct-image
   assertion (resp. its complex form) holds for $f_0j_0$ and $f_0i_0$,
   it holds for $f_0$.
1. *(Target.)* Let $j'_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be open with closed
   complement $i'_0:T_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$, and let
   $f_{V}:f_0^{-1}(V_0)\to V_0$, $f_T:f_0^{-1}(T_0)\to T_0$ be the
   restrictions of $f_0$. If the direct-image assertion (resp. its
   complex form) holds for $f_V$ and $f_T$, it holds for $f_0$.
   By induction, the same holds for any finite stratification of $Y_0$
   by locally closed pieces built from successive open–closed
   decompositions.
1. *(Coefficients.)* Fix $f_0$ and $w$, and let
   $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ be an exact
   sequence of constructible Weil sheaves on $X_0$. If
   $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F'$ and $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F''$ are $\iota$-mixed
   of weights at most $w+r$ for every $r$, so is $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$.
   By induction on the length, the same holds for a finite filtration of
   $\mathcal F$ by Weil subsheaves.

proof.text: Use the finite-field, $\Qlb$, embedding $\iota$ and weight conventions of [def-weil-punctual-weights] and [def-weil-complex-weights]. Work with the common-stage coefficient categories and fixed-pair Weil objects of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. A triangle of Weil objects here means an underlying distinguished triangle with Weil-equivariant arrows; no triangulated structure on the category of fixed pairs is assumed. First observe that if $A\xrightarrow a B\xrightarrow b C$ is exact at $B$ in constructible Weil sheaves and $A,C$ are mixed of weights at most $u$, then $B$ has that bound. Indeed $I=\operatorname{im}a$ is a quotient of $A$, and $B/I\cong\operatorname{im}b$ is a subobject of $C$. Clause (1) of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] bounds both; clause (2) applies to $0\to I\to B\to B/I\to0$.

For any locally closed $h_0:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0$, clause (1) of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] says $h^*$ is exact and identifies closed-point Frobenius stalks with the same residue field. Apply $h^*$ to the finite pure-quotient filtration in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Its quotients remain pure of the same weights, since their Frobenius eigenvalues and $q_x$ are unchanged; remove repeated filtration terms if necessary. Thus $h^*$ preserves mixed bounds. The cohomology comparison in that clause then gives $\mathcal H^a(h^*K)=h^*\mathcal H^a(K)$ with bound $w+a$ for every $a$ whenever $K\in D_{\le w}$. By [def-weil-complex-weights], $h^*K\in D_{\le w}$.

Clause (2) of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] makes $j_!$ exact on constructible Weil sheaves and gives its Frobenius-equivariant stalk formula. Extend a pure-quotient filtration by $j_!$: exactness identifies its successive quotients with the extensions by zero of the original quotients. Inside $U_0$ the eigenvalues and residue-field sizes are unchanged; outside $U_0$ there are no eigenvalues, so the purity condition is vacuous. Thus each quotient is pure of its original weight in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Consequently $j_!$ preserves upper mixed bounds. Since $\mathcal H^a(Rj_!L)\cong j_!\mathcal H^a(L)$, it also preserves $D_{\le w}$ by [def-weil-complex-weights].

For the source decomposition, apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ to $K$ and the complementary immersions after base change to $k$. Its equivariance clause applies because $j_0,i_0$ descend to $k_0$. Apply $Rf_!$, the exact functor with Weil lift in [prop-weil-operations]. Clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] gives the triangle
$$R(f_0j_0)_!j_0^*K\longrightarrow Rf_{0!}K\longrightarrow R(f_0i_0)_!i_0^*K\longrightarrow.$$
All terms are bounded constructible and all maps are Weil-equivariant by these cited statements. Here and below the schemes are separated of finite type and $\ell\ne p$; thus the $\Qlb$ bounded constructible domains in the package apply, without the additional hypotheses of its smooth-base-change clause.

For the complex source assertion, take $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$. Step 2 and the two assumed complex assertions put the outer terms $A=R(f_0j_0)_!j_0^*K$ and $C=R(f_0i_0)_!i_0^*K$ of step 4 in $D_{\le w}(Y_0)$. Apply clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] to the underlying distinguished triangle in the common-stage coefficient category. For every integer $a$ it gives an exact segment $\mathcal H^a(A)\to\mathcal H^a(Rf_{0!}K)\to\mathcal H^a(C)$. The triangle is Weil-equivariant, and the cohomology maps are equivariant by [prop-weil-operations]. By [def-weil-complex-weights], the outer sheaves have bound $w+a$. Step 1 with $u=w+a$ bounds the middle sheaf. Since this holds for every $a$, [def-weil-complex-weights] gives $Rf_{0!}K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$. This is the degreewise extension-stability argument in the stated common-stage category; no comparison with another coefficient category is used.

For the sheaf source assertion, take $K=\mathcal F[0]$ in step 4. Clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], applied in the underlying standard constructible heart, gives the exact segment
$$R^r(f_0j_0)_!j_0^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F\longrightarrow R^r(f_0i_0)_!i_0^*\mathcal F.$$
The naturality of cohomology and the equivariance of the triangle, supplied by [prop-weil-operations], make this an exact segment of Weil sheaves. Step 2 bounds both restricted input sheaves by $w$, and the assumed sheaf assertions bound the outer direct images by $w+r$. Step 1 with $u=w+r$ bounds the middle term, for every $r$.

proof.text:
For the target decomposition use the Cartesian squares over $j'_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ and $i'_0:T_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$. Their source maps are complementary immersions into $X_0$. Clause (4) of [prop-functor-package] gives
$$j_0'^*Rf_{0!}K\cong Rf_{V!}(K|_{f_0^{-1}V_0}),\qquad i_0'^*Rf_{0!}K\cong Rf_{T!}(K|_{f_0^{-1}T_0}).$$
These are morphisms of Weil complexes by [prop-weil-operations]. We use arbitrary base change for $Rf_!$ at the $\Qlb$ bounded constructible stage, not smooth base change for $Rf_*$. The restricted morphisms are separated finite-type morphisms since they are obtained by base change from $f_0$. For $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$, step 2 and the two assumed complex assertions bound both right sides by $w$.

Put $M=Rf_{0!}K$. Step 7 bounds $j_0'^*M$ and $i_0'^*M$ by $w$. Step 3 bounds $j'_{0!}j_0'^*M$ by $w$. The closed immersion $i'_0$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] (Stacks Tag 035C), so [lem-zl-finite-pushforward] bounds $Ri'_{0*}i_0'^*M$ by $w$. The two outer terms therefore satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-zl-open-closed-weight], which yields $M\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$. This proves the target complex assertion.

For the target sheaf assertion put $K=\mathcal F[0]$ in the base-change isomorphisms of step 7 and write $G=R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F$. Clause (1) of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] allows taking $\mathcal H^r$ through both target pullbacks. Thus $j_0'^*G$ and $i_0'^*G$ identify with $R^rf_{V!}(\mathcal F|_{f_0^{-1}V_0})$ and $R^rf_{T!}(\mathcal F|_{f_0^{-1}T_0})$. The input restrictions have bound $w$ by step 2, so these sheaves have bound $w+r$ by the assumed sheaf assertions. Apply the reassembly argument of step 8 to $G[0]$ with bound $w+r$: step 3 bounds its open extension and [lem-zl-finite-pushforward] bounds its closed direct image, then [lem-zl-open-closed-weight] bounds $G[0]$. The degree-zero case of [def-weil-complex-weights] says precisely that $G$ is mixed of weights at most $w+r$.

For a finite target stratification built by successive open--closed decompositions, induct on its finite decomposition tree. At a leaf the required direct-image assertion is the assumed assertion on that stratum. At an internal vertex its two child assertions imply its assertion by steps 7--9 applied to the corresponding restriction of $f_0$. Repeating up to the root gives the assertion on $Y_0$. The empty piece contributes only the zero functor, and a one-piece stratification is the hypothesis itself.

For the coefficient assertion forget to the underlying constructible heart. Clause (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] turns the given short exact sequence into an underlying distinguished triangle; its connecting morphism is natural, and therefore commutes with Frobenius. Apply the exact Weil-lifted functor $Rf_{0!}$ from [prop-weil-operations], then clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. For every $r$ this gives an exact Weil segment $R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F'\to R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F\to R^rf_{0!}\mathcal F''$. Its outer terms have bound $w+r$ by hypothesis, so step 1 bounds the middle term. For a filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F$, start with the zero sheaf and apply this argument successively to $0\to\mathcal F_{a-1}\to\mathcal F_a\to\mathcal F_a/\mathcal F_{a-1}\to0$. It proves the assertion when every graded piece has the assumed direct-image bounds.
